response.explanation: Processes are created with `mp_context.Process`, where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`. That returns a `SpawnProcess`. `_ensure_processes_alive` and `join` guard `kill()`/`terminate()` with `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. `multiprocessing.Process` is the default-context class, and `SpawnProcess` does not subclass it. The check is therefore False for every real flusher process, so `kill()` is skipped. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. When a process is restarted because it is hung (cause "hang"), the old process stays alive and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second one for the same shards. The same check in `join` means `process.terminate()` is skipped at shutdown. I did not run this; it follows from CPython's class layout.
response.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed because isinstance check uses the wrong Process class
